prompt: Match each Svelte idea with its name in React.
hint: The table in the first section.

prompt: Match each Svelte idea with its name in Vue or Angular.
hint: Vue's names are in its single-file components; Angular's are functions and decorators.

prompt: What does the lesson say a table of matching names hides?

choices.text: That two of the frameworks cannot build the planner
choices.why: Each of the other courses builds the same planner.

choices.text: The licence each framework is published under
choices.why: Licences do not come up in the lesson.

choices.text: When code runs and what each framework knows
choices.why: Right: the rest of the lesson is about those differences.

choices.text: Which of the four frameworks is the oldest one
choices.why: Age is not one of the differences the lesson takes up.

prompt: What is React's counterpart to a keyed `{#each}`?
hint: An array method and a prop.

choices.text: `.map()` returning elements with a `key`
choices.why: Right: the key tells React which item is which, as in Svelte.

choices.text: `useMemo` around the list of elements
choices.why: `useMemo` saves work; it identifies nothing.

choices.text: `v-for` with a `:key` on each element
choices.why: That is Vue's.

choices.text: `@for` with a `track` expression
choices.why: That is Angular's.

prompt: Put the four counter builds in order, from the least compressed JavaScript to the most.
hint: Two of them are close to each other.
trap: Vue and Angular are 4 kB apart; React is more than twice either.

prompt: How many kB, compressed and rounded to the nearest whole number, did the Svelte counter's build send?
What is almost all of each number in the comparison?

choices.text: The router that each application framework adds
choices.why: These are client-only builds, with no application framework.

choices.text: The HTML page, inlined into the JavaScript bundle
choices.why: `index.html` is a separate file of a fraction of a kilobyte.

choices.text: The counter component's own compiled code and its markup
choices.why: The counter is a few lines; the numbers are far larger.

choices.text: The framework's runtime, needed before any component
choices.why: Right: it is the floor every page with that framework stands on.

prompt: Why does the lesson say the gap between Svelte and the others narrows as an application grows?
hint: Compare what grows on each side.

choices.text: The other frameworks remove their runtimes in large builds
choices.why: Nothing removes a runtime the components need.

choices.text: The app's own code soon outweighs any runtime
choices.why: Right: the fixed floor matters less as the rest grows.

choices.text: Gzip compresses Svelte's output less well the more of it there is
choices.why: The lesson says nothing of the sort.

choices.text: Svelte's runtime gets larger with every new route
choices.why: The runtime is the fixed part; it does not grow per route.

prompt: Why was the Angular counter built with Angular 21 rather than 22?

choices.text: Version 21 made the smallest bundle of the two
choices.why: Nothing was compared between Angular versions.

choices.text: Angular 22 asks for a newer Node 22 than the catalogue's
choices.why: Right: so the counter used the newest Angular this Node runs.

choices.text: Angular 22 has dropped support for signals
choices.why: Signals are where Angular is heading, not what it dropped.

choices.text: Angular 22 cannot produce a production build yet
choices.why: It builds; it would not install on this Node.

prompt: When `minutes` changes in the React counter, what runs again?

choices.text: Only the effect that sets the paragraph's text
choices.why: That is Svelte's compiled effect.

choices.text: Nothing until the page is reloaded by the browser
choices.why: React updates the page without a reload.

choices.text: Only the `useState` call, and not the rest
choices.why: Everything in the function body runs on every change.

choices.text: The whole `Counter` function, then a comparison
choices.why: Right: React compares the new description with the old one.

prompt: Why do React's rules of hooks exist, according to the lesson?
hint: How does React tell two `useState` calls apart?

choices.text: The call order tells one `useState` from the next
choices.why: Right: since the function runs again each time, the order has to stay the same.

choices.text: Hooks may be called only in the browser, never on a server
choices.why: The lesson says nothing about where hooks may run.

choices.text: A hook that is not called first slows every render down
choices.why: Speed is not the reason given.

choices.text: Hooks are compiled away, and the compiler needs them at the top
choices.why: React has no compile step that removes hooks.

prompt: Why does the lesson call Vue's way a middle position?
hint: Precise about one thing, comparing in another.

choices.text: It runs half its components on the server and half in the browser
choices.why: Where components run is not what the lesson compares here.

choices.text: It mixes the Options API and the Composition API
choices.why: Those are ways of writing components, not of updating them.

choices.text: It knows which component changed, then compares within it
choices.why: Right: precise about which component, comparing within it.

choices.text: It has signals like Svelte's but no compiler at all
choices.why: Vue's compiler marks the parts of a template that never change.

prompt: The library Angular grew up with, which noticed every event and timer and then checked every component, is ___.js.
Match each SvelteKit file or feature with its Next.js counterpart.
Which of the other three has come closest to SvelteKit's forms that work with JavaScript off?

choices.text: Nuxt, through its server routes in `server/`
choices.why: Those are called with `$fetch`, from code in the page.

choices.text: Angular, through `HttpClient` and reactive forms
choices.why: Those send data with JavaScript.

choices.text: Vue, through `v-model` on every input
choices.why: `v-model` binds a value in the browser; it sends nothing.

choices.text: React, with Server Actions in Next.js
choices.why: Right: they can be submitted before the page's JavaScript has loaded.

prompt: What kind of difference does the lesson say the forms row is?
hint: Any of the four can build the planner either way.

choices.text: A difference in the browsers each framework supports
choices.why: Browser support does not come up.

choices.text: A difference of default, not of capability
choices.why: Right: the default decides what most projects end up with.

choices.text: A difference of speed under heavy load
choices.why: Speed is not what the row is about.

choices.text: A difference of capability that cannot be built around
choices.why: The lesson says any of the four can build it.

prompt: Which lesson of this course built the planner's forms that work with JavaScript off?
hint: It was the longest in the course.

prompt: Which of these does the lesson count among Svelte's costs? Choose all that apply.
hint: Three costs, each with its own bullet.

choices.text: A smaller ecosystem of libraries
choices.why: Right: for Svelte there may be one library where React has several.

choices.text: Fewer people who already know it
choices.why: Right: a team hiring for React draws from a larger pool.

choices.text: Changes between versions, such as runes
choices.why: Right: lesson 4 exists because of them.

choices.text: More JavaScript sent to the browser
choices.why: The counter measured the opposite.

prompt: Where does the lesson say Angular's structure earns the most?

choices.text: A form that must keep working with JavaScript switched off
choices.why: That is SvelteKit's default.

choices.text: A small site where the first load on a slow phone matters
choices.why: That is where Svelte's defaults earn the most.

choices.text: A large organisation's app, kept for a decade by many teams
choices.why: Right: one framework and one way to do things helps there.

choices.text: A project that depends on a library written for React
choices.why: That project is served by React.

prompt: A colleague says the counter comparison shows Svelte apps stay seven times smaller than React apps at any size. What is wrong with that?

choices.text: They measure the runtime floor, not how an app grows
choices.why: Right: a counter measures the floor, not how an application grows.

choices.text: Gzip was applied to Svelte's file but not to React's
choices.why: Both are compared compressed.

choices.text: Nothing: the ratio holds for applications of any size
choices.why: The lesson says the gap narrows as an application grows.

choices.text: The React build was made in development mode
choices.why: All four were production builds.

prompt: You move to a Vue team. Which thing from this course has the most direct counterpart there?

choices.text: `$derived`, which Vue calls `computed`
choices.why: Right: a value worked out from others, recalculated when they change.

choices.text: `$props`, which Vue calls `input()`
choices.why: `input()` is Angular's; Vue's is `defineProps`.

choices.text: Form actions, which Vue calls Server Actions
choices.why: Server Actions are React's, in Next.js.

choices.text: `use:enhance`, which Vue calls `v-enhance`
choices.why: There is no such directive; Nuxt sends data with `$fetch`.
